protocol: Within one scan the rail anchors past a cut are hidden, TrackGeometry.path is called on the retained anchors, and its prediction is scored against the hidden anchors. Two alternatives are scored on the same hidden anchors: a local quadratic arc, and a straight line whose slope is least-squares fitted over a 20 m window instead of the last two anchors. No odometry, annotations or cross-frame registration are involved. Hidden anchors are the rail-pair detector output, whose per-step search is bounded to rail_max_heading around the previous anchor, so reported errors are lower bounds. Anchor centres are quantised to rail_bin_m/2 = 0.015 m.
conclusion: No recording in this subset carries measurable curvature: the observed track centre grows linearly with range in all six (rms of a straight fit 0.004-0.046 m, a quadratic term adds nothing), which is a sensor-to-track yaw offset, not a curve. The endpoint tangent already predicts the held-out anchors better than either alternative, so replacing it with an arc is refuted on this data and was not implemented.
